properties.name: Usage telemetry carries the verb and never the object — what was called, never what it was called on
properties.statement:
WHEN REFLOW2 REPORTS ITS OWN USAGE FROM A HOSTED DEPLOYMENT, THE PAYLOAD CONTAINS WHAT WAS CALLED AND NEVER WHAT IT WAS CALLED ON. Tool name, skill name, outcome class, duration — yes. Node ids, statements, search queries, error messages quoting user text, tool arguments — no.

ANTHONY'S FRAMING, 2026-08-09, and the constraint is his: if he and Alex get flo2 (a web app around reflow2) running at ~1,000 users, usage statistics become the instrument for improving reflow2 — \"BUT NOT ON THE USER'S CONTENT, AS I DON'T WANT TO BE ACCUSED OF TAKING THEIR DESIGNS.\"

⭐ THE LINE IS SHARPER THAN \"NO CONTENT\", AND IT HAS TO BE, BECAUSE THE LEAKS ARE NOT WHERE PEOPLE LOOK. A node id IS design content — `req:the-ledger-can-say-the-record-was-wrong` announces its own intent. A SEARCH QUERY is content and is the worst offender, because it names the user's domain in their own words. An ERROR MESSAGE is content whenever it quotes the input: \"unknown change type: correction\" is safe; \"node not found: cmp:secret-cooling-loop\" is not. TOOL ARGUMENTS are almost always content. So the rule that actually holds is: **LOG THE VERB, NEVER THE OBJECT.**

⭐⭐ A STRUCTURE THAT CANNOT CARRY CONTENT BEATS A POLICY PROMISING NOT TO. If the payload is a fixed, published schema whose every field is enum-valued or numeric — tool name from the served set, outcome from a known set, duration as a bucket — then it is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of carrying a design, and that is demonstrable to a suspicious customer rather than merely asserted. A free-text field anywhere in the payload defeats this no matter what the policy says, because the next contributor will put something useful in it. This is the same move reflow2 makes everywhere else: make the honest thing COMPUTABLE rather than PROMISED.

--- WHAT THE STATISTICS MAY AND MAY NOT DECIDE ---

Anthony named two uses. They do not carry equal weight and the difference is already recorded in this design.

(1) A TOOL USED ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE MORE THAN OTHERS → OPTIMISE IT. Sound, and it needs LATENCY as well as counts: call volume alone does not say what is slow.

(2) A TOOL RARELY OR NEVER USED → CUT IT OR IMPROVE ITS USEFULNESS. ⚠️ **THIS IS `dec:bl-155`'S TRAP AT SCALE, AND IT IS ALREADY MEASURED HERE.** That instrument found 40 of 132 tools never called, and its central finding was that **reflow2 CANNOT TELL \"unused\" FROM \"unreachable\"**. Its group (c) was the uncomfortable one: reads that answer real questions on designs that exist today, which nobody reaches for — `evidence_report` gained three axes in a release and appears in NO SKILL. A tool nobody can FIND is indistinguishable from a tool nobody WANTS.

⇒ **USAGE COUNTS MAY JUSTIFY OPTIMISING. THEY MAY NOT, ALONE, JUSTIFY CUTTING.** Cutting on raw counts removes exactly the capabilities that were never surfaced, and does so with the confidence of a number. The discoverability question — is this tool named by any skill, nudge or report? — must be answered before a removal, and that question is answerable from the shipped build without any telemetry at all.

--- WHY THE SHAPE MUST BE MULTI-TENANT NOW, NOT LATER ---

`rule:no-foreclosure` (Anthony, 2026-07-25) forbids taking a shortcut today that makes it impossible to become a hosted multi-user service, and names identity-in-a-global and config-that-widens among the specific foreclosures. A telemetry design that assumes one tenant is a NEW foreclosure of exactly that kind. Per-tenant separation, and an aggregation threshold below which a cohort is not reported at all, belong in the first version even while there is one user — they cost nothing now and are expensive to retrofit.

AND THE DEPLOYMENT MUST BE ABLE TO SAY NO. A self-hosted or air-gapped consumer must be able to run with telemetry off entirely. `rule:no-foreclosure`'s clause (4) applies directly: per-request configuration may only ever NARROW what the deployment allowed, never re-include what was excluded.

RELATED, ALREADY OPEN, AND NOT DUPLICATED: `dec:idea-measure-the-surface` asks whether real usage telemetry should be a standing instrument and HOW FAR IT MAY GO. This requirement answers the second half — how far — and leaves the first to that decision. `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` holds the mechanism and storage question.
